issue_context.title: Unify BufferedFileStreamStrategy seeking
issue_context.body:
Today while trying to find an answer to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/discussions/78390 I've realized that `BufferedFileStreamStrategy` has two different approaches to seeking.

`Seek` provides a smart way of seeking that tries to avoid losing the buffered data if possible:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/031a16ae6797e3ee0ebf718364a533a76b9083bc/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/Strategies/BufferedFileStreamStrategy.cs#L936-L946

While `Position` setter is plain simple and always loses the buffered data:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/031a16ae6797e3ee0ebf718364a533a76b9083bc/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/Strategies/BufferedFileStreamStrategy.cs#L66-L77

`Position` should be "smart" too and most likely just delegate the work to `Seek`

review_comments:
`BufferedFileStreamStrategy` is used when buffering is enabled (`bufferSize > 1`), but when it's disabled then a class that derives from `OSFileStreamStrategy` is used.

`OSFileStreamStrategy.Seek` verifies that an existing content of a file opened for append is never overwritten by setting the file position:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/372adbf8a4fcfe788e8f0fca3ed0fb9423099a76/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/Strategies/OSFileStreamStrategy.cs#L170-L175

`OSFileStreamStrategy.Position` does not perform such check:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/372adbf8a4fcfe788e8f0fca3ed0fb9423099a76/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/Strategies/OSFileStreamStrategy.cs#L88

So we can't use `_strategy.Position` here.
Is this introducing any new failure modes, things set_Position wouldn't throw for but Seek would?

You are right, it does :
```
EnsureNotClosed();
EnsureCanSeek();
```
which throws exceptions.

Should I implement saving buffered data inside Position setter instead of reusing Seek code ? and refactor (if possible) to not deduplicate same code between Position and Seek ?
I'll leave that up to @adamsitnik, whether we want to just delegate or try to do something special.
